subject: Benchmark ride‑along & evidence exchange — acceptance metrics and next steps
body:
From: Tom Perez <tom.perez@latticehealth.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@latticehealth.com>, EngOps <engops@latticehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark ride‑along & acceptance metrics

Hi Monica / Ben —

Thanks for the call this morning. Priya and I talked through the acceptance checklist and have a small set of clarifications before we sign off the mutual action plan (MAP). High level asks:

- Confirm the target 95th-percentile tail latency threshold (we currently see 95th ~ 220ms in preprod; your note said 180ms).
- Confirm what counts as a failed run for the ride‑along (errors vs token-level hallucinations vs latency breaches).
- How will Redwood capture telemetry during the ride‑along? We need raw per-request traces (request_id, model_version, seq_len, latency_ms) exported for our audit team.

We attached the load script we’ll run (lh-loadscript-v2.yml) and our current telemetry snapshot. Can you confirm an owner for post-run artifacts?

Thanks —
Tom
Sr. Eng Manager, LatticeHealth

-----Original Message-----
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Sent: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 08:05:12 -0700
To: Tom Perez <tom.perez@latticehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai; Priya Singh <priya.s@latticehealth.com>
Subject: Benchmark ride‑along & evidence exchange — acceptance metrics and next steps

Tom / Priya — great to meet you today. Below is the agreed plan and owners for the onboarding benchmark ride‑along. I’ve included assumptions and what counts as acceptance artifacts.

Summary (agreed on call):
- Scope: 1-hour ride‑along followed by 2-hour debug window (Redwood + Lattice EngOps).
- Targets: 95th percentile latency <= 180 ms; median latency <= 60 ms; sustained throughput 150 req/s for 3k tokens average payload. Error rate < 0.5% (server 5xx / EOS exceptions).
- Warmup: 20 minutes of progressive traffic (10%, 30%, 60%, 100%) to populate KV caches.
- Telemetry: Redwood will export per-request traces + aggregated token cost breakdown. Export format: JSON lines with request_id, timestamp, model, model_version, seq_len, latency_ms, outcome_code.
- Acceptance artifacts: telemetry export, run log, loadscript, a short summary doc with top 5 latency outliers and root cause notes.
- When: Wed Jun 9, 09:00–12:00 PT (ride‑along 09:00–10:00, debug 10:00–12:00).

Owners:
- Redwood owner (evidence & postrun): monica_patel — will collect telemetry, upload artifacts to the shared Drive, and post the summary.
- Redwood ops lead (oncall during run): ben_carter — will monitor GPU utilization, autoscaler, and accept fallback policies.
- CS/Implementation: marissa_cole — will run through the MAP checklist and coordinate signoff.
- Lattice owners: Tom Perez (Eng), Priya Singh (EngOps) — will run their load agent and validate acceptance artifacts on their side.

Artifacts attached: lh-loadscript-v2.yml (load profile, concurrency targets), MAP-LatticeHealth-acceptance.pdf (signed draft).

Please reply with any last changes; otherwise Ben and I will post the telemetry contract and the Drive link by EOD.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jun 7, 2027 at 11:34 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:

Monica / Tom / Priya — quick note from infra: we will enable prefix caching with a 45‑minute TTL for this run and pin the model to redwood-gpt-7b-v2-quant (as discussed). Two small asks:
1) Confirm that Lattice can limit client-side sequence lengths to <= 3k tokens for the scheduled run. If you need spikes above that we need to adjust batch sizing and kernels.
2) Please ensure the load agents include request_id in the X-Request-ID header so we can stitch traces.

I’ll standby as ops lead during the window.

—Ben
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jun 7, 2027 at 12:02 PM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai> wrote:

Following up with the MAP checklist and signoff flow. I’ve attached the draft MAP PDF and added a short acceptance checklist below. Can someone from Lattice confirm acceptance criteria inline?

Acceptance checklist (simple):
- Latency: 95th ≤ 180ms (PASS / FAIL)
- Throughput: sustain 150 req/s for 10 continuous minutes at 100% concurrency (PASS / FAIL)
- Error rate: < 0.5% per run window (PASS / FAIL)
- Artefacts: telemetry export + run summary uploaded to shared Drive (YES / NO)

If all PASS/YES we move to final signoff and post the DocuSign link for the production enablement contract.

—Marissa
Implementation Lead — Redwood Inference

On Wed, Jun 9, 2027 at 09:03:11 -0700 Tom Perez <tom.perez@latticehealth.com> wrote:

Monica / Ben / Marissa — we ran the window. Highlights:
- Warmup behaved as expected (cache warmed at 18 minutes).
- Sustained 150 req/s for 12 minutes; median latency 58 ms; 95th 195 ms (outlier cluster during minute 9).
- Error rate 0.4% (mostly short timeouts from a misconfigured client retry loop on our side).

Attached: lh-telemetry-snapshot-20270607.json (sampled), and the loadscript we used.

Immediate asks:
- Can Redwood annotate the 9th-minute outlier cluster with kernel-level metrics (GPU queue depth, batch sizes)?
- Please confirm if we consider the run PASS/FAIL given 95th at 195ms vs target 180ms (we understand this may be attributable to our client retry loop spike).

—Tom

On Wed, Jun 9, 2027 at 10:22:05 -0700 monica_patel@redwood.ai wrote:

Tom / Priya — thanks for running this and for the quick notes. Preliminary read:
- We agree the primary cause for the 95th tail bump is a brief client-side retry storm that created microbursts and larger batches; Ben is pulling kernel traces now.
- We propose a remediation path and decision cadence:
  1) Redwood to post annotated latency outlier file with kernel metrics within 6 hours (owner: ben_carter).
  2) Lattice to confirm client retry fix and re-run a focused 30‑minute validation window within 48 hours.
  3) If re-run passes the checklist, Redwood will mark the onboarding acceptance as PASS and proceed to DocuSign for production enablement.

Action items assigned in the shared MAP doc. I’ll upload artifacts to the Drive and post the link here when ready.

Thanks —
Monica
